steps.text: Thursday

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Please, take a seat, Melanite. Make yourself comfortable. I believe this is the first time you've proactively come to me for a session?

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: ...Yes.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Relax. We're just here to chat. Is there anything in particular that you want to talk about?

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: I'm been having... dreams.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: What kind of dreams?

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: I don't remember the details. All I remember is that I had a dream... and the lingering feelings pressing down on my chest.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: No memories of the dream itself... lingering feelings... When did this start?

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: About a week ago. The sensation is getting stronger and lasting longer, sometimes even all day...

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Are they nightmares?

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: The only nightmare I ever have is of that night. Of watching the rioters approach my father, but somehow I just can't pull the trigger like he taught me to.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: I would wake up sweating, my heart hammering against my chest. But since I know it's not real, I can quickly calm myself down.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: But these recent dreams... it's different. It's hard to describe, but it feels like having a piece of cotton-padded lead in my arms; soft, but heavy.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Heavy... so heavy, and the feeling lasts for so long... It's hard for me to concentrate.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Do you have any medication I could take for it?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Medication may not be the answer. I suspect your dreams involve faded memories, maybe something from your childhood you've forgotten. Do you think you'd be comfortable talking about your parents?

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Sure.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: I thought you would be more... reticent.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: No, not at all.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: My father used to work for Blacksteel. He had a medium, stocky build, was missing an arm, and had a little moustache.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: My mother was a housewife who worked part-time doing laundry before Dad retired, then the two of them ran the shop together. She was a little taller than my father, lanky. That's all.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: What about yourself?

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Me? I was a kid. I did kid things.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Can you talk about yourself in more detail?
Melanite looks up at the yellowish light on the ceiling.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: ...More detail?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: I went to school, helped out at home and around the shop, and played with the neighbors' kids. That's about it.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Any unforgettable memories? Sights, experiences, that sort of thing.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Nothing worth mentioning.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Well, I'd like to hear them anyway, even if it doesn't seem relevant. Anything that comes to mind.
Melanite looks around at the room's furnishings.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: The light back home was yellow, just like this one. The flooring wasn't so nice, and would creak every now and then.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: The table was really high... or maybe I was just too small at the time.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: What about yourself? What did you do or think back then?

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Me?

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Oh, I had a scar on my knee that faded away at some point. The staircase at home must've been pretty high for me to fall.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: The light, the floor, the table, the stairs... Oh, and... the chairs.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: The chairs were...

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Melanite...

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: I don't quite remember, but I think they were made of wood—

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: That's enough, Melanite.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Uh.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: You're just stating facts without context or emotion. Like you're talking about somebody else.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Those are just my impressions from back then.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Only facts, with no details or emotions, not even your own place in the scene... It must be hard for you.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: No, not at all.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: How so?

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: I want to forget what happened that night... but it all comes back so vividly whenever I have one of those nightmares.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: If I forget what happened before all that, then at least I can be indifferent. At least I can...

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: I'd feel less bad about losing something I don't care about.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: The life I have now has nothing to do with what happened back then. Whatever I feel or don't feel about it, it won't affect me at all.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Melanite...

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Sorry that I kept talking about things unrelated to the dreams. I guess if you don't have any pills I can take, I'll try to adjust on my own.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: No, it could be related. Maybe resolving your issues with your childhood memories will also help with—

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Sorry for worrying you. I should be going.
Melanite turns around, avoiding Honeyberry's concerned gaze, and walks out of the room.
She meant to go straight back to her dorm, but took a wrong turn out of anxiety and ended up in an unfamiliar corner.
Seeing an empty hallway, she instinctively puts her hand on her railgun's trigger, before realizing it and moving her hand away.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: This is Rhodes Island. Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Even if you've never been here before, there's nothing you can't deal with... Everything here is safe. Really.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Nothing in your past has anything to do with you, Operator.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: No one here will hurt you. You're well compensated and receive proper treatment, as long as you can deliver sufficient fire support in battle.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: It's alright, it's alright...
Melanite takes a few deep breaths.
Talking to herself, taking deep breaths... How much these techniques help is debatable, but they can't hurt.
The anxiety that had climbed up her calves recedes back to her ankles.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: It's okay, it's okay... Just act normal, business as usual.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: It has nothing to do with you. Detach yourself. It'll all get better.
Friday

steps.name: Medical Department Operator
steps.text: Your regular checkup is complete, Operator Melanite. It'll be a while before the report is ready, though.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Okay.

steps.name: Medical Department Operator
steps.text: Is something bothering you?

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: How... How did you...

steps.name: Medical Department Operator
steps.text: Er... 'how did I' what?

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: I-I mean, how did you know something's bothering me? Did something come up in the checkup?

steps.name: Medical Department Operator
steps.text: No, I just thought you looked really pale.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: ...I guess I didn't sleep well last night. Had a dream.

steps.name: Medical Department Operator
steps.text: Alright, the report's ready. Let me see...

steps.name: Medical Department Operator
steps.text: Hmm... Oripathy symptoms are stable, but there are various changes in other areas.

steps.name: Medical Department Operator
steps.text: Looks like it's true that you've been sleeping poorly. Nightmares?

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: ...No, just ordinary dreams, really. I even had a chat with Honeyberry about them yesterday. I'm perfectly fine, and ready to work.

steps.name: Medical Department Operator
steps.text: Work? What does work have to do with any of this?

steps.name: Medical Department Operator
steps.text: Here, have some chocolate. It'll help you settle down.
Melanite takes the unwrapped chocolate, looking deep in thought. She takes a bite, and a bitter-sweet taste fills her mouth.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: ...Will my condition affect my next field mission?

steps.name: Medical Department Operator
steps.text: Well, it's a little concerning. If you haven't gotten better by then, I would recommend a period of rest.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Rest...?

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: No, I'll be fine by then.

steps.name: Medical Department Operator
steps.text: Well, I'm glad you're confident, at least.

steps.name: Medical Department Operator
steps.text: I'm heading to lunch. Care to join me?

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Er, thanks, but not today.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: ...I need to get better.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: How did I used to do it?

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: I used to keep myself busy enough that my mind didn't have time to wander.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: It'll get better.
Saturday

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Instructor Dobermann.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Today's Saturday. Are you sure you don't want to take a day off?

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: No need.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: I'd welcome that kind of motivation if this were the problem children of A6, but you're the type to keep pressuring yourself without accepting anybody's help.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Plus, the results from your checkup yesterday weren't too good.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: I even had a little conversation with Honeyberry about you. I can't say I fully understand, but it's clear that you've been bothered by your dreams lately.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: You knew?!

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Keeping track of your condition is part of my job as instructor.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: I'm fine, Instructor. Really.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Did you have another dream last night?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Take the day off.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Please, training is the best way for me to relieve stress.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Are you sure?

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: I'm sure.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Missed.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Missed.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Missed!

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: This isn't working at all...

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: I've done this so many times before, but I've never missed like this...

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: The more I try to aim, the more my hand shakes. What's going on? How do I fulfill my duties like this?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Time's up!

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: I'm sorry... I let everyone down.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: It's solo training. Who exactly are you letting down?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Come on, have some warm milk.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: What I mean is... I'll only be a burden on missions if this keeps up.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: You don't need to worry about that.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: You mean... operators in poor condition won't even be sent on missions?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: To put it bluntly, yes. Field missions can be dangerous.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: And an operator in bad form can't be trusted with them?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Sorry, but I need to go. Thanks for the milk.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Melanite? Melanite!
Sunday
As she opens her eyes, she feels the familiar sensation of the dream filling her chest for a fleeting moment.
If she takes a moment to savor it, the soft yet heavy feeling seems almost poignant.
It is not the bloody pain of having your arm cut off.
It is the sorrow of remembering, long after the injury has healed, that you once used your hands to cover a friend's eyes one afternoon, long ago.
Now, however, Melanite does not have the luxury of analyzing the subtle and difficult-to-describe emotions.

All she knows is that her dreams have disrupted every aspect of her life, made her anxious, given others cause for concern and made them give her special treatment... Left unchecked, they would eventually make her a worthless invalid.
Rhodes Island may be kind, but how long would they tolerate an invalid?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Why would you think like that, Melanite? That's not how his works!

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Is it not?

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: My relatives supported me because we're connected by blood.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: They greeted me warmly because my grades were good.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: My previous employer paid me because I could test weapons that others couldn't.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Rhodes Island employs me and gives me treatment because I can provide fire support with this railgun...

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: I know it's disrespectful to compare you to them, but who would help a worthless invalid?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: ...Your parents.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: They loved you unconditionally, didn't they? Otherwise, why would you be so upset about losing them?

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Just stop right there, Honeyberry, please. All I want is a quiet and peaceful life. I don't need unconditional love. It's enough that I can earn a living with my own two hands.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: You can't allow... No, you can't pretend that the memories of the past are but a distant shadow, just because you feel sad when you remember them.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Maybe your subconscious defensive mechanisms are detaching you from your past emotions without you even realizing it. But that doesn't mean they've gone away.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: They're just tucked away in a corner, hidden from your consciousness. But you can't remain detached and run away forever.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: If you're worried about these dreams ruining your life, then running away will only make it worse.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: But... what can I do? I can't go on like this.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Rhodes Island doesn't fire people just because they have mental health issues. You can trust me on that.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Maybe people need a reason to love someone, but you certainly don't need one to show kindness.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Just spend the rest of the day doing whatever you want, okay?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: I'll get you something to drink. There are books here, if you want to read.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: 'The warm air rising from the cup melted the white frost on the window. The subtle, tender scent calmed my mind...'

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: 'Firewood cracked in the fireplace opposite the armchair, seemingly causing the air in the room to rise and expand, like soft bread...'

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: No... I can't even read a book.
Melanite brings the cup of warm cystymilk towards her mouth.
Before it touches her lips, the poignant sensation in her chest suddenly grows sharply.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: (The smell of cystymilk? I had a little bit when I was with Instructor Dobermann, too...)

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: (No, it's not just cystymilk... there's something else.)

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: (But why would I feel like there's something else? Have I smelled something recently?)

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: (Maybe... there's something near my room?)

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Honeyberry, I... I need to step out for a bit.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Sure. I'll be here all day. Come back anytime you want.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: (Here it is, my room... There's a faint smell... but it's not coming from inside. It's from over there...)

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: (Here it is. Just one floor from my room.)

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: (The smell's coming from that unremarkable door in the corner. I can probably find out what's going on by going inside.)

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: (But what if...)
What if whatever's inside makes you feel like a fool?
You and I, we worked so hard to forget those painful memories... Unconsciously, you shoved all those colors, smells, and emotions onto me and detached yourself.
Just so you could feel better, so you wouldn't think back to happier times when you're alone, so you could clench your teeth and keep going.
Go back, Melanite. There's nothing to see here. You don't know, but I do, and it's absurdly simple.
Emotions, memories, they're nothing more than burdens to you.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: But I'm already at my limit.

Don't believe those people. Did you really think you would get better? They're just doing the job they're paid for, whispering sweet lies into your ear. What do they care what happens to you afterwards?

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Then what do you want me to do?
Go back.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: I need to... I need to know what I'm dreaming about.
What if what's inside doesn't have anything to do with your dreams, or your past, or your life?

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: You said you knew!
Do you really want to let all our efforts over all these years go to waste?
Are you really going in?
Melanite pulls the door open.
The voice like her own no longer speaks, instead merging into the smell coming from the room.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: ...Instructor Dur-nar?

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Melanite?!
Dur-nar is holding a hot drink in her hands.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: This smell...

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: What are you doing here? Did Medical send you?

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: No... I just smelled something like a drink.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Whew, you gave me a fright there.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: So what is it?

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: A kind of powdered drink mix with milk. Real nutritious. It used to be carried in grocery stores all across Columbia about a decade ago, but you can hardly find it all these days. Took a lot of effort to get my hands on this.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: But you can have some if you want. I haven't touch this cup yet.
Melanite takes the cup with a blank look on her face, feeling the warmth in her hands and trying to pinpoint the deep sorrow that the sweet scent has stirred within her heart.
The memories float to the surface, but years of evasion have made their surface cold and smooth.
She tries to reach towards the source of the sorrow that seems so incongruous with the sweetness, yet it lingers just out of reach.
She takes a sip of the light brown liquid in the cup.
As her tongue senses the sweetness, those memories dissolve in water, with the sweet scent of chocolate and cystymilk emanating from the surface.
In the reflection, she sees herself holding a warm drink in her hand.
In the cup, she finds the time that she lost, and is found in turn by the time she once thought discarded.
She hears an unfamiliar yet familiar voice from the cup.

steps.name: Father's Voice
steps.text: Look at this, Breonna.

steps.name: Father's Voice
steps.text: This drink powder is selling like crazy. This was the last box, and people kept asking me to sell it, but... this one's for my little girl, and it's not for sale.

steps.name: Father's Voice
steps.text: What's the matter? You're just holding the cup.

steps.name: Mother's Voice
steps.text: That's because the cystymilk's still too hot for her. Isn't that right, Breonna?

steps.name: Breonna
steps.text: Yeah, it's too hot!

steps.name: Breonna
steps.text: I'm waiting for it to cool down!
Two faint silhouettes with the scent of chocolate and cystymilk emerge from the vapor.

steps.name: Father's Silhouette
steps.text: You always liked Daddy's guns, right Breonna? C'mon, let's head out of town and—

steps.name: Mother's Silhouette
steps.text: She's eight, you dumb oaf!

steps.name: Father's Silhouette
steps.text: Look, I've only got the one hand, and it's holding the gun. It's not even loaded, not a single etched bullet.

steps.name: Mother's Silhouette
steps.text: Fine, fine, but at least let her finish her drink.
Then, places that had long been reduced to mere words in Melanite's memory.

steps.name: Breonna
steps.text: I thought you didn't bring any etched ammo, Daddy.

steps.name: Father's Silhouette
steps.text: Just because your Daddy only has one arm doesn't mean he can't hide something when he puts his mind to it.

steps.name: Father's Silhouette
steps.text: Here, I'll hold your hand. Focus on the feel of casting...

steps.name: Father's Silhouette
steps.text: Whoa, you're a natural! Took me half a month to fire my first shot.

steps.name: Father's Silhouette
steps.text: But you still need practice. Shooting a gun isn't easy, and without practice, you might not be able to pull it off when it counts.
Finally, all the haziness begins to clear up.
The carefree childhood she must have had emerges from the teacup with shades of brown and white, along with the Breonna from before she became Melanite.

steps.name: Father
steps.text: I thought that powdered drink would keep selling, but I guess it was just a fad. Now it's all just sitting in the storeroom.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: We can't cut the price any further, but it's taking up so much space.

steps.name: Father
steps.text: *Sigh*...

steps.name: Breonna
steps.text: I-I like it! I'll drink it every day!

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Breonna?
Her father was more than just a stocky man with one arm and a moustache. He could be impulsive, but he loved his little girl dearly, partly out of guilt for not being there for her as an infant.
Her mother was more than just a lanky housewife. Everything in the household revolved around her firm voice and deft hands. She was strict with her daughter, but just as loving.
As for Breonna... She grew from a young child filled with questions about everything when her father first came home, to a girl only a little shorter than her father.
At some point she stopped getting taller, but she thought those days would continue forever.

steps.name: Father
steps.text: That's the last of the drink... Have you been drinking even more when we're not looking? That's a lot of calories to work off, you know.

steps.name: Father
steps.text: But thanks to you, we managed to turn our losses around and keep this little grocery store going. You're our lucky star.

steps.name: Father
steps.text: We'll always love you, no matter what. And we'll always be together.

steps.name: Father
steps.text: Goodnight, Breonna. Dream a dream of chocolate.
Goodnight, Breonna. Dream a dream of chocolate.
With that, her father went downstairs. And after that bloody night, she locked all that sweetness away in a forgotten corner of her memories, whether consciously or unconsciously.
What she lost was so precious that she had wished she never had it.
Until now.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Melanite? Are you ok? Are you... crying?

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: (Fights back sobbing)

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: I-It's okay, Instructor, I just... I remembered what I had forgotten...
Monday

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: (Blows nose) I feel so happy for you, Melanite.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: By the way, I was asked to deliver something to you.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: To me?
Melanite takes out a little cardboard box.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: The assorted dried berries from Rim Billiton that Instructor Dur-nar promised you.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Oh? Have you started working for Dur-nar's Snack Network?

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: Yup.

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: To remember even more lost flavors, and recall more lost memories...

steps.name: Melanite
steps.text: To bring back the time I lost.
